subject: optimizer law: native Chuck step in both trainers, notorch pin advanced

submodule.pin_after_subject: Reuse the existing microkernel and validate each copied boundary before measuring the native vocabulary projection.

contract.reads_gradients_from: tape entry e->grad, identical to nt_tape_adam_step
contract.loss_val_use: feeds only the Chuck loss controller: loss_ema (0.99/0.01), a 16-slot loss window, the quartile trend with brake/push at +-0.02, stagnation noise after 8 flat steps, and a macro EMA patience that scales lr every 1000 steps
contract.per_call_semantics: one call is one Chuck step for every window and counter; accumulated application is therefore well defined when the caller performs exactly one call per accumulated batch
contract.state_reset: nt_tape_destroy() memsets the whole tape, so reset_optimizer() in both trainers clears Chuck global and per-parameter state together with the moments
notes: a parameter whose gradient norm stays under NT_CHUCK_FREEZE_THRESH (0.01) for 8 consecutive steps is frozen permanently inside this function; nothing in the step unfreezes it
the stagnation-noise RNG is a file-static in notorch.c and is not reset by nt_tape_destroy, so its stream continues across optimizer resets within one process
windows need 8 recorded steps before any adaptation, so the first steps of a short run move like the diagonal baseline with dampen 1.0 and lr_scale 1.0

call_sites.loss_val: v, the example cross-entropy already checked finite on the line above
dpo, the pair loss being minimized; the backward runs on the weighted surrogate whose value is not a loss

call_sites.stage: joint objective, one accumulated step per epoch
call_sites.loss_val: (float)sum, that epoch's online joint loss as printed in online_mean_objective_ce for the joint route

call_sites.stage: batch route, one step per microbatch

tests.coverage_limit: the suite does not execute the four swapped call sites. test/head.c, test/mlp.c, test/optimizer.c, test/weighting.c and test/joint.c include the trainers with main renamed and drive their own update loops with nt_tape_adam_step as the oracle, so identical before/after output proves the swap broke nothing those tests check, not that the trainers behave the same

claims_not_made: no claim that Chuck and the diagonal baseline produce equivalent training outcomes on any corpus
no claim about loss, transfer or checkpoint quality under the new step: nothing was trained in this change
no claim that the joint route's accumulated single step is the best granularity for the Chuck controller, only that it matches the contract
